Each task asks the agent to add a capability to an existing open-source library or service, specified the way a series of pull requests would be, while every existing behaviour keeps working.
The data pipeline tasks extend data libraries so pipelines keep producing correct results after an upstream format or schema change.
Hidden tests check the new behaviour and the old behaviour together.
Gemini 4 Argon passes 11% of its runs on these tasks, and it fails every run on 85% of the tasks.
Gemini 3.8 Flash passes 0%, and it fails every run on 98% of the tasks.
The main languages are Go (68%), Python (32%) and C# (1%).

| Domain | What the tasks do | % of catalog |
|---|---|---:|
| Languages & developer tooling | Add features to command-line tools, compilers and API tooling. | 22% |
| Systems, hardware & accelerators
Maintainers add a capability that runs through many code paths of an unfamiliar library or service, while existing callers must see no change.
Typical requests add an opt-in mode or policy, keep information the library currently drops, or make a subsystem safe under concurrency and failure.

Data engineers face a related problem: after an upstream format or schema change, a pipeline keeps running but produces wrong results, and the library has to handle the new data while old inputs still work.
Each task pins an open-source repository, mostly Go or Python, in an offline container and gives a written specification of the new behaviour, with the public types and functions to deliver.
The agent's edits are collected as a diff against the base commit.
After the session, hidden acceptance tests check the new behaviour and the project's existing tests check that nothing else changed.
The data pipeline tasks also provide sample inputs in `/data`.
A capability gap stated as "X cannot Y", then dense paragraphs on the behaviour to add and the behaviour to preserve.
A bullet list of required exported names, constants and signatures, with a research and plan file due before any code change.
A first-person data problem after an upstream change, with sample files in `/data` and a request to keep existing results unchanged.
